question: Should OpenClaw add a per-target-agent subagent concurrency config surface for this use case, and if so what public shape and scheduler model should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public configuration and queue semantics that overlap with broader lane-concurrency requests, so automation should not choose the API shape alone.

options.title: Add scoped per-target cap
options.body: Use the existing namespace pattern, likely `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent`, and enforce it as an additional target-agent cap while preserving the global subagent lane cap.

options.title: Fold into broader lane design
options.body: Treat this as part of the larger subagent lane work so per-target limits and named lanes share one public model.

options.title: Reject new config surface
options.body: Keep only the global subagent cap plus current per-requester active-child limit and document that target-specific serialization is not supported.

recommendation.title: Add scoped per-target cap
recommendation.body: Use the existing namespace pattern, likely `agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent`, and enforce it as an additional target-agent cap while preserving the global subagent lane cap.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing trail points to the existing concurrency resolver and gateway lane applier ownership.
